amenitiesDescription:
The clubhouse: Four thousand square feet given over to a residents' lounge, a library and a conference room with high-speed Wi-Fi — programmed for people who work from home as much as for entertaining.

Pool and wellness: A resort-style pool deck with sunbed relaxation areas and a plunge pool, alongside an athletic centre.

The village itself: Gardens, plazas, walkways and fountains between the homes, with glorietas drawn from the 1929 Ibero-American Exposition. The Villas carry their own heated pools, outdoor kitchens and showers.

Services: On-site management, a 24-hour monitored HD camera system, guest parking and electric vehicle charging stations.

investmentIntelligence.thesis: The Village is Coral Gables' eighth village and the completion of a plan George Merrick set out a century ago — forty-eight Spanish-colonial homes on a single 2.6-acre block of gardens, plazas and fountains, with nothing above four stories. The scarcity argument is the assembly cost: six transactions and $15.85 million in 2022, plus a unanimous commission vote, which is why projects of this scale stay uncommon in Coral Gables. The building has already proved its ceiling, setting the city's new-construction record at $1,675 a square foot in February 2025, and it has already delivered. What remains is six finished homes from $2.55 million — priced as completed product, with the delivery, financing and construction risk that defines the rest of this market entirely removed.

investmentThesis:
Blocks of this scale are uncommon in Coral Gables. The site took six separate transactions and $15.85 million to assemble in 2022, a unanimous city commission vote to approve, and a Mediterranean Revival density bonus of two extra units per acre. No comparable assemblage is currently in the pipeline. Whatever the market does, the supply at this address is fixed.

The building has already proved its ceiling. Villa 4 closed at $4.8 million in February 2025 — $1,675 per square foot, the highest ever paid for new construction in Coral Gables. Forty-two of the forty-eight homes are sold, the project topped off ahead of schedule in November 2024 at 60% sold, move-ins began in Summer 2025, and the final phase handed over in Spring 2026.

What is left is six residences at Phase 3 pricing: two Villas at $4.5 million, two Townhomes at $3.99 and $4.2 million, and two Lofts at $2.55 and $2.7 million. A buyer here is not underwriting a delivery date, a construction loan or a rendering — the homes are standing, landscaped and occupied by neighbours. That is a materially different risk profile from everything else on this site, and it is priced as finished product rather than as a pre-construction discount.

name: The Village at Coral Gables
residenceContent:
Seventeen lots bounded by Malaga Avenue, Santander Avenue, Segovia Street and Hernando Street, assembled into a single 2.6-acre block and built out as Coral Gables' eighth village. De La Guardia Victoria Architects & Urbanists drew it as a piece of town rather than a building — tree-lined streets, plazas, walkways and fountains between the homes, with glorietas modelled on the 1929 Ibero-American Exposition. Nothing rises above four stories. The whole enclave completes the plan George Merrick set out for the City Beautiful a century ago, which is the point of it.

Forty-eight residences across four collections. Twenty-four Flats of two bedrooms and a study, 1,698 to 1,771 square feet of interior space under ten-foot cove ceilings, each with a covered loggia. Four three-story Lofts at 1,881 square feet, with fourteen-foot cathedral ceilings over the primary bedroom and a private two-car garage. Sixteen three-story Townhomes from 3,147 to 3,246 square feet, with wet bars, walk-in laundries, skylights over the stairs and private elevators from the garage. Four two-story Villas at 2,439 and 2,863 square feet, each with a heated pool, an outdoor kitchen with gas grill and an outdoor shower.

The specification is the same throughout: hurricane-rated CGI windows and doors in a bronze finish, wood-plank front doors, Italian kitchen cabinetry with stone counters and backsplash, Wolf and Sub-Zero appliances, natural stone bathroom floors with Italian double vanities in stained wood, seven- and eight-foot premium wood doors, coral stone on every terrace, smooth painted stucco and brown clay barrel roof tile outside. Air conditioning runs in zones, hot water recirculates, and every home is generator-ready and wired for an electric vehicle charger.
tagline: Forty-eight Spanish-colonial residences on a 2.6-acre block in the heart of Coral Gables — built, landscaped and handed over.
